To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the N = 18 and N = 20 shell closures are preserved in light neutron-rich nuclei, while the N = 22 shell closure is strongly reduced and the N = 24 and N = 26 shell closures are almost completely removed in these nuclei.

the spherical N = 20 shell closure is found in all N = 19 isotones, while the N = 22 and N = 24 shell closures are found to be deformed and that the N = 26 shell closure is found for N - Z = 10 and N = 27.

the spherical N = 28 magic number disappears for N - Z > 10 in the light neutron-rich nuclei, and is replaced by deformed magic numbers, while the spherical N =20 magic number is preserved for all N =20 isotones, but becomes dynamically deformed in 32Mg.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of the shell structure of neutron-rich nuclei and the isospin dependence on the nuclear mean field.
the evolution of the N =20 and N =28 shell closures in the vicinity of the doubly magic 32Mg nucleus.
